name: Miyamoto Usagi
summary: Stan Sakai's rabbit ronin: Miyamoto Usagi, a masterless samurai on a warrior's pilgrimage through an animal version of feudal Japan. Star of Usagi Yojimbo since 1984.
origin: Usagi grew up the only son of a village headman. As a boy he watched the wandering master Katsuichi easily defeat a gang of students from the Dogora sword school, and he stood outside Katsuichi's home day and night until the master agreed to teach him. After winning a Dogora tournament he became a retainer and later bodyguard of Lord Mifune. When a rival lord's war ended in betrayal at the battle of Adachigahara, Mifune died, and Usagi escaped with his lord's head so the enemy couldn't display it. Now a ronin, he wanders as a bodyguard for hire.
powers: Master swordsman, one of the best in the land
Daisho swords Yagi no Eda and Aoyagi

storyline.title: Albedo Anthropomorphics
storyline.beat: Usagi first appears in the anthology Albedo Anthropomorphics #2 from Thoughts and Images.

storyline.title: Anthology years
storyline.beat: He moves to Fantagraphics' anthology Critters before getting his own series in 1987.

storyline.title: Adachigahara
storyline.beat: Betrayal at the battle of Adachigahara kills Lord Mifune, leaves Usagi with his scar and sets him wandering.

storyline.title: Ninja Turtles crossovers
storyline.beat: Usagi becomes a regular guest in the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles franchise, in comics and across several cartoons.

storyline.title: Four publishers
storyline.beat: The series moves from Fantagraphics to Mirage, Dark Horse and IDW, then returns to Dark Horse in 2023.

storyline.title: Samurai Rabbit
storyline.beat: Netflix's Samurai Rabbit: The Usagi Chronicles follows his descendant Yuichi, with Usagi appearing on the side.

gossip.text: Sakai based Usagi on the legendary swordsman Miyamoto Musashi.
Usagi was going to be human until Sakai doodled a rabbit with its ears tied up like a samurai topknot.
The series title comes from Akira Kurosawa's 1961 film Yojimbo. Usagi is Japanese for rabbit.
Sakai also letters Groo the Wanderer, and won a 1996 Eisner for lettering Groo and Usagi Yojimbo.
Sakai and the series have collected a whole shelf of Eisner Awards, many of them for lettering.
Usagi Yojimbo started out as a Ninja Turtles spin-off.
gossip.truth: Usagi debuted in 1984 in Albedo Anthropomorphics. He only joined the Turtles franchise later as a guest.

quiz.why: Sakai drew on the life of Miyamoto Musashi.

quiz.q: Which franchise does Usagi most often cross over with?
quiz.why: He has appeared alongside the Turtles in comics and several cartoons.

theme.tagline: Long ears, longer road, the fastest blade in the province.

timeline.title: Albedo Anthropomorphics #2
timeline.note: Stan Sakai's rabbit ronin first appears in the November 1984 issue of an indie anthology.

timeline.title: His own series
timeline.note: Fantagraphics launches the Usagi Yojimbo ongoing series in July 1987.

timeline.title: First Eisners
timeline.note: Sakai and the series collect their first two Eisner Awards.

timeline.title: Grasscutter wins
timeline.note: The Grasscutter arc takes the Eisner for Best Serialized Story.

timeline.title: Moves to IDW
timeline.note: IDW picks up the series with a new monthly run.

timeline.title: Samurai Rabbit
timeline.note: Netflix's animated series premieres in April, following Usagi's descendant Yuichi.

timeline.title: Home to Dark Horse
timeline.note: Usagi returns to Dark Horse in September and also joins TMNT: Shredder's Revenge as a playable character.
